author: r. d. golden
title: Medicaid spending for Evaluation and Management services in Sylva reaches $5,793,383 in 2024
text:
In 2024, Medicaid providers in Sylva billed $5,793,383 for services under the Evaluation and Management category, data from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Medicaid Provider Spending database shows. This total is a 15.3% uptick from 2023, when claims for this service category amounted to $5,026,515.
Medicaid is a government health insurance program operated by states and funded jointly at the state and federal level. The program serves low-income residents, older adults, children and people with disabilities, making it a central part of the U.S. health system.
Because taxpayer funds support Medicaid, shifts in local billing levels reflect community allocation of public health spending.
The “Evaluation and Management” category includes Medicaid-billed services defined by the care provided and grouped by standardized HCPCS and CPT codes. For this analysis, each code was assigned to exactly one service category based on consistent prefixes and number ranges to allow analysis of related services, prevent double counting and maintain accurate rankings across years.
Spending rose across several Medicaid service categories, with Evaluation and Management ranking as the second-highest by total Medicaid payments in Sylva in 2024.
Statewide in North Carolina, Evaluation and Management also placed second by total Medicaid payments in 2024.
Between 2019 and 2024, Medicaid spending tied to the Evaluation and Management category in Sylva grew by $3,458,294—a 148.1% increase. Some years saw rapid growth, particularly during 2021 and 2022.
While Evaluation and Management payments occurred throughout Sylva, they were concentrated in a small number of ZIP codes. In 2024, ZIP code 28779 accounted for $5,793,382 in Medicaid payments for the category, representing 100% of such payments in the city that year.
Claims within the Evaluation and Management group were largely concentrated among a select group of billing codes.
To compare, Medicaid payments for Evaluation and Management in Sylva rose 15.3% from 2023 to 2024, while the rise across all Medicaid claim groups in Sylva during that time was 21.3%.
According to the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, federal and state Medicaid outlays reached roughly $871.7 billion in fiscal 2023, making up about 18% of total national health spending—a significant increase from about $613.5 billion in 2019 before the COVID-19 pandemic.
This growth reflects an approximately 40% rise in spending in a few years, attributed mainly to increased enrollment and higher service use during and after the pandemic.
Recent federal budget actions under the Trump administration have proposed major reductions to federal Medicaid funding and structural changes to the program. The “One Big Beautiful Bill Act,” enacted in 2025, is expected to cut over $1 trillion from federal Medicaid spending over the next 10 years, and introduce policies like work requirements and greater cost-sharing, potentially reducing coverage and funding for some groups. These adjustments are anticipated to place more burden on states and limit the pace of federal support, while the program continues to serve many Americans.
